subject: Egress identity profiling, firewall contract and evidence handoff
messages:
From: Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@aegishealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Aegis Health Procurement <procurement@aegishealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Private endpoint: egress identity profiling + firewall contract

Sergio — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked for two specific items before we move to contract: a concise list of outbound IPs/hostnames your private endpoint will use for the control plane and an explanation of how you portray outbound identity (SNI, TLS client certs, source IP, etc.).

Can you also confirm whether Redwood can sign a short firewall annex that maps to our security questionnaire (we'll share the template)? We want to confirm there are no dynamic, hard-to-audit egress channels and to capture rotation windows for ephemeral IPs.

I've attached a starter inventory we've prepared (aegis-egress-inventory.xlsx) — it's lightweight. If you can respond this week we can keep procurement moving.

Best,
Mike
Director of Cloud Ops
Aegis Health

Attachment: aegis-egress-inventory.xlsx (xlsx stub)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoint: egress identity profiling + firewall contract

Mike — appreciate the list and the clear ask. Quick summary up front:
- Control plane egress: small set of static IPs (regional), plus optional ephemeral pool for burst; we can commit to a static control-plane CIDR block for the contract.
- Data plane (model inference) traffic: routed over customer network (private), no outbound to public internet except for image/kms endpoints when using Managed Private.
- Identity signals: primary = TLS client certs (mutual TLS) + SNI for routing; source IP is authoritative for allowlist but we also support a per-tenant TLS certificate fingerprint in the console for added assurance.

We can sign a firewall annex that: pins control-plane IPs (or a documented process for ephemeral IP rotation), documents mTLS requirement, and defines the rotation/notification SLA. I'll loop Laura for the annex text and Karthik for any infra caveats.

Action items: Laura will draft the annex and Karthik will produce a true egress-IP list and the rotation cadence. Expect the draft tomorrow.

—Sergio
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@aegishealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@aegishealth.com>, Aegis Health Procurement <procurement@aegishealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoint: egress identity profiling + firewall contract

Thanks — helpful. Two clarifying items from our security team below: 

1) Ephemeral IPs: acceptable only if you provide a signed weekly rotation manifest and a push notification to our security mailbox 72 hours before change.
2) Evidence: we need a snapshot showing that mTLS is enforced end-to-end for control-plane calls (short PDF is fine), plus any SOC2 or pen-test artifacts that validate egress controls.

I've attached the SOC2 snapshot we have on file for our vendors; if Redwood can provide a short statement and the mTLS snapshot by Monday we can avoid a drawn-out audit.

Regards,
Alice
Security Engineer, Aegis Health

Attachment: requested-soc2-snapshot.pdf (pdf stub)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@aegishealth.com>, Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoint: egress identity profiling + firewall contract

Alice / Mike — thanks for the specifics. Deliverables (timeline):

1) Egress IP manifest: CSV + signed manifest. Includes regional static pool (control-plane): 52.143.10.0/28 (primary), 52.143.11.0/28 (failover). Ephemeral pool: zonal ephemeral range with documented rotation window (30–90 min bursts) — we'll provide rotation manifest weekly. ETA: Mon 2026-11-22 EOD.

2) mTLS evidence: short runbook and a single-run capture (curl + OpenSSL output) showing client cert negotiation and fingerprint. Will redact keys and include the cert fingerprint and SNI patterns. ETA: Mon 2026-11-22 EOD.

3) Firewall annex draft: Marissa will attach a 1-page annex that maps to your questionnaire fields (allowed IPs, rotation SLA, mTLS requirement, audit contact). ETA: Tue 2026-11-23.

Notes / clarifications:
- We will not require outbound internet access from your inference layer for model requests — control-plane is the primary egress vector for telemetry/metrics.
- If you require a deterministic signed IP set (for your hardware firewall appliance), we can provide a signed JSON manifest and GPG signature on cadence you choose.

I'll send the three deliverables as separate attachments next week; Marissa will coordinate the annex review with your procurement counsel.

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0192

Attachment stubs to follow: egress-manifest.csv, mtls-evidence.txt, firewall-annex-draft.pdf
